stories.headline: Congress politics of accusation and deceit .... Attempt to malign the Election Commission
stories.title: Congress politics of accusation and deceit .... Attempt to malign the Election Commission
stories.summary: Congress has called the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls a plot to that the party's own 1993 record with Chief Election Commissioner T.N. Seshan weakens its claim to defend the Commission's independence. Rahul Gandhi and his party have found a new villain to prove that they are still relevant as opposition. It is the Election Commission of India. They say the Special Intensive Revision of the electoral rolls is a plot. They call it "vote chori". They say it robs citizens of their vote. Some of them even want the Chief Election Commissioner to resign. It is a loud campaign. It is also a short-sighted one. Congress is the last party that should lecture anyone on the independence of the Election Commission. Its own record tells a different story. The man who scared them Go back to 1990. T. N. Seshan became Chief Election Commissioner. He did what few before him had dared. He enforced the Model Code of Conduct without fear. He cracked down on booth capturing. He stopped ministers from using government machinery to win votes. He made photo identity cards a reality. Politicians hated him. Every party felt the heat. But it was the Congress government at the Centre that acted. In 1993, the government of P. V. Narasimha Rao changed the structure of the commission. It had always been led by one man. Now it would have three members. The two new commissioners had equal powers. Decisions would be taken by majority. Look at the timing. Seshan was at the peak of his influence. The government was tired of being told no. Seshan saw the move for what it was. He went to the Supreme Court. The court upheld the new structure in 1995. The three-member commission stands to this day. Congress may call this reform. Most people who watched at the time called it an attempt to clip the wings of a strong umpire. The party that now cries foul Now compare that with today. Congress leaders speak as if they have always been guardians of the commission. They call it a puppet. They compare their struggle to the fight for freedom. They demand resignations. Where was this love for institutions in 1993? When an independent chief election commissioner became inconvenient, Congress cut him down to size. When the commission does a routine job today, Congress screams conspiracy. That is the definition of double standards. What SIR really is Let us be clear about what this exercise is. The revision of electoral rolls is not new. The law requires it. Its purpose is simple. Remove the names of the dead. Remove duplicate entries. Remove people who have moved elsewhere. Add new voters who are eligible. India is a vast country. People migrate for work. They marry and change homes. They die, and their names stay on the list for years. Any honest clean-up will remove many names. That is not a scandal. That is the job. The commission has said again and again that a wrongly deleted voter can apply to be added back. Booth Level Officers are available in every area. Online portals are open. Citizens can check their entries and correct them. So ask the Congress a plain question. If your voters are being deleted, where are the names? Where are the cases? Show them to the commission. Show them to the courts. A slogan is not evidence. What about those bogus voters, the Guspethias who were crying on the top of their voices, standing at the India-Bangladesh border, crying that we want to go back & we have voted in India several times but now we have to go back as the things have changed & more than 180 km of open borders will be sealed soon. Everyone saw those long queues of Guspethias patronised by TMC & Congress waiting to go back... The question they cannot answer Here is the biggest hole in their argument. They say names are being deleted to help the BJP. But how would the commission know who votes for whom? The voter list has no column for party choice. There is no tag that says "Congress voter". The ballot is secret. That is the whole point of it. To delete opponents on purpose, someone would have to know who they are. Congress has never explained this. It cannot. The theory falls apart the moment you think about it for a minute. Voters are not fooled The public is not buying it. Talk to ordinary people, and you hear the same thing. They want clean rolls. Fewer fake names mean a fairer contest. That helps every honest party. Many voters have already fixed their own entries. They went to the Booth Level Officer or used the online portal. They found it slow at times, but it worked. They do not feel like victims of a plot & are not buying Congress's baseless allegations. Assam is a good example. The state saw the same claims from Congress. Once the Election Commission explained the process, the allegations lost their force. Union Minister Pabitra Margherita made the point well when he said Assam had rejected Congress on SIR. Baseless attacks on institutions, he said, had become part of a political culture. People are tired of it. Every time Congress loses, it finds a new reason. First it was the voting machines. Now it is the voter list. Never once does it ask what went wrong in its own campaign, its own organisation or its own message. The cry that lost its meaning "Democracy is in danger," Congress says it before every election and after every defeat. Each time, the words mean a little less. Democracy was in real danger when the Emergency was imposed in 1975. Newspapers were censored. Opposition leaders were jailed. Courts were pressured. That was done by a Congress government. The party has no right to use the language of democratic crisis whenever it wants a headline. A mature opposition would do the hard work. It would send its workers door to door. It would find real errors and file real complaints. It would go to court with names and numbers. That is how a serious party behaves. Shouting "vote chori" from a stage is not the same as proving it. What the BJP believes Those are reasonable demands. The BJP has no problem with them. We want every eligible Indian to vote. We also want every fake name gone. No Guspethias to do bogus voting. What we reject is the idea that any clean-up of the rolls is an attack on democracy. It is the opposite. A dirty voter list is what weakens democracy. A clean one protects it. On appointments, the law of 2023 set up a selection panel that includes the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition and a Union minister. The Leader of the Opposition has a seat and a voice at the table. That is a long way from the old practice, under which the government of the day simply picked the chief. Congress used that old practice for decades and never once complained. Consistency is the test Institutions do not survive because they are free from criticism. They survive because they are judged by one standard, no matter who is in power. Congress fails that test. It cut down a strong commissioner when it held the Centre. Now it attacks the commission because it lost elections. It praises the umpire when it wins and abuses him when it loses. If Congress truly cares about the Election Commission, it should start with honesty. Admit what happened in 1993. Bring evidence, not slogans. Fight elections with ideas and work on the ground. Until then, its outrage will sound exactly like what it is. It is a party looking for someone to blame. (The author is a spokesperson for the BJP. stories.headline: US, Israel must abandon path of confrontation: Dr Farooq Abdullah
stories.title: US, Israel must abandon path of confrontation: Dr Farooq Abdullah
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 6: The Jammu and Kashmir National Conference President, Dr Farooq Abdullah, Tuesday expressed deep concern over the ongoing crisis in West Asia, saying that the conflict has engulfed not only the region but has also had repercussions across the world. He appealed to all peace-loving countries, particularly Arab and Muslim nations, to utilise all available diplomatic and political avenues to help bring the present crisis to an end. "International institutions, including the United Nations and the International Court of Justice, should also play an effective role in facilitating reconciliation, dialogue and negotiations between the parties so that the region can be saved from further destruction. At the same time, Israel must be held accountable for alleged war crimes and genocide in Palestine," he said. Dr Farooq, as per a party statement, said that the United States and Israel must abandon their war-driven approach and make the protection of civilians and their lives and property their foremost priority. “War can never provide a permanent solution to any problem, and the use of force only aggravates the humanitarian tragedy,” he said. He also expressed deep regret over missile attacks by Houthi rebels towards the Holy cities of Makkah and Madinah. He said targeting or threatening the sacred places with any form of attack was deeply regrettable and had hurt the sentiments of Muslims across the world. He urged the Houthi leadership to refrain completely from such actions.

stories.headline: Nifty 50 companies likely to log strong double-digit growth in Q2
stories.title: Nifty 50 companies likely to log strong double-digit growth in Q2
stories.summary: Mumbai: Aggregate revenue and net profit of the Nifty 50 companies are expected to grow in double digits year-on-year for the September quarter led by select companies from the automobiles, banking and finance, metals and oil and gas sectors. Revenue and net profit are likely to grow by 19.9% and 22.3% respectively according to the ETIG estimates. Their performance will also benefit from the lower base of 9% and 8.4% growth in revenue and profit in the year-ago quarter."The broader earnings outlook remains healthy, supported by improving domestic demand, strong credit growth, government spending and a recovery in private capex," said Feroze Azeez, Joint CEO, Anand Rathi Wealth.134753222Gautam Duggad, MD and Head of Sales, Institutional Equities, Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) expects Nifty earnings to grow by 27% and that of the companies covered by the broking firm to increase by 22%."Excluding oil marketing companies, aggregate earnings for the MOFSL Universe are expected to grow 24% year-on-year during the quarter," Duggad said.Read more: How a 9-year-old Warren Buffett learnt a lesson on compounding by rolling snowballs on the lawn of his Nebraska homeThe operating margin at the aggregate level is likely to contract by a tad 20 basis points to 21.9% from the year ago amid input cost inflation. Azzez expects margins to remain mixed as benefits of lower commodity costs are normalising while wage inflation and higher crude prices are creating some pressure on margins. "For capital goods, infrastructure and manufacturing, margins likely to remain stable to improving, supported by healthy order books, capacity utilisation and operating leverage," he mentioned, adding that for banking and finance companies, earnings growth would be driven more by strong loan growth than by expansion in margins.Read more: Why junk bonds deliver equity-like returns but with far inferior volatility, explains Saurabh MukherjeaDespite near-term challenges in the form of volatile energy prices, geopolitical and tariff risks, and weakening rupee against major currnecies, analysts are optimistic about medium-to-long term growth trajectory. Duggad believes that the risk-reward for Indian equities over a medium and long term has meaningfully improved given healthy earnings growth, resilient macroeconomic environment and cooling valuations. "With earnings growth increasingly concentrated in select themes, we expect market performance to remain firmly bottom-up, favouring growth-oriented businesses that are successfully scaling up and strengthening their competitive positioning," Duggad said. He expects 15-16% earnings growth over FY26-28 for the companies under his coverage.Azeez of Anand Rathi remains constructive for FY27 driven by strong healthy domestic demand and credit growth, government and private capital expenditure, and improving corporate earnings. "For FY27, Nifty 50 earnings per share (EPS) is expected to rise to ₹1,240 from ₹1,088 with 14% earnings growth," he said.Sector viewAutomobilesDemand across automobile segments remained resilient with sales volume growing in double digits year-on-year in the September quarter, barring lower tractor volume amid irregular monsoon. While revenue of majority of the auto makers is expected to rise in double digits, profits and profitability may remain muted due to higher input costs.BankingNet interest income is expected to grow in low double digits year-on-year while non-interest income may decline amid lower treasury income due to firm bond yields. Net interest margin may show weakness depending upon the extent of FCNR deposits raised by banks. The asset quality is likely to stay stable.Capital GoodsFresh orders from segments including power generation, transmission and distribution, data centres, and infrastructure kept the order book ringing during the quarter. While domestic execution gained pace amid scattered monsoon trend, geopolitical disturbance in the West Asian region may result in slower order ramp up. Higher raw material costs will weigh on profitability though the impact may soften due to pass-though of higher costs in some projects.CementCement demand is expected to grow in higher single digit in the September quarter, helped by sustained construction activities in an otherwise seasonally weak quarter due to monsoon. Demand was steady in the North, Western and Central regions. Cement prices showed a gradual recovery, largely to offset higher input costs. However, profitability is likely to remain under pressure.FMCGBarring ITC, fast moving consumer goods (FMCG) companies are likely to report double digit revenue growth amid stable sales volume, higher product prices and low base in the year ago quarter. ITC is expected to show weaker sales volume, which is expected to result in lower revenue and profit for the quarter.Information TechnologyClients continued to observe caution while ramping up large, discretionary assignments. This is expected to keep top line growth muted for most top tier IT companies. The sequential revenue growth for the top tier companies is expected to remain under 2-3% for the quarte keeping currency rates constant. Operating margins may show a slight uptick in the absence of major wage increases for most of the top companies. Over 8.7% depreciation in the average rupee rate against the dollar during the quarter will support the rupee-denominated performanceMetalsElevated prices of aluminium, copper, and zinc are expected to help non-ferrous companies to post strong performance in the September quarter. Ferrous companies, too, are expected to benefit from firm domestic demand from the infrastructure segment.PharmaceuticalsCompanies with domestic focus are expected to show continued traction in the September quarter while US focused pharma companies such as Dr Reddy's Labs and Cipla are likely to report weakness with a double-digit drop in revenue. A weaker rupee is expected to soften the blow in reported profits.

stories.headline: Chief Justice calls for technological sovereignty, justice for farmers
stories.title: Chief Justice calls for technological sovereignty, justice for farmers
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 6: Addressing a special session of the 60th Diamond Jubilee Convention of the Indian Society of Agricultural Engineers (ISAE) at Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir (SKUAST-K), Shalimar, the Chief Justice of the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati, called for ensuring that technological advancement in agriculture is accompanied by protection of farmers’ digital, economic and legal rights. The three-day Diamond Jubilee Convention, hosted by SKUAST-K, brought together nearly 700 agricultural engineers, scientists, technocrats and students from India and abroad. The convention focused on themes including ‘Women Leading Engineering Innovations in Smart Farming’ and ‘AI and Robotics for Gen-Z Farming’. “Today, every soldier—whether it be a farmer, a scientist, a teacher, a lawyer, or a judge—will have to be equipped with that kind of technology,” he said, drawing a parallel with the changing nature of modern warfare and the increasing use of drones and other advanced technologies. Earlier, the Chief Justice visited the exhibition stalls set up outside the auditorium and reviewed technologies related to drip irrigation, crop monitoring and drone-based agricultural applications. He stressed the need to make such technologies accessible and understandable to farmers so that they can effectively adopt them. Speaking during the session, Vice Chancellor, Prof Nazir A Ganai SKUAST-K, highlighted the need to accelerate technological interventions in agriculture to unlock the sector’s untapped potential. He said while the Green Revolution helped India overcome food shortages, the country now needs to focus on technology, skilled human resources and innovation to address emerging agricultural challenges. The Vice Chancellor also underlined concerns related to technological and data sovereignty in agriculture, particularly with the increasing use of drones, sensors and digital platforms. He stressed that farmers’ rights must extend beyond markets, land and water to the digital domain as well. The technical sessions featured addresses by Shri N.S. Rathore, Former Vice Chancellor, MPUAT, Udaipur, and Former Deputy Director General (Education), ICAR, on “AI-Driven Agricultural Technology, Smart Skills & Advanced Agricultural Techniques”, and Prof. V.P. Singh, Distinguished Professor, Texas A&M University, USA, on “Mathematical Modelling of the Water-Energy-Environment-Food Nexus.” The session also highlighted the research and innovation ecosystem of SKUAST-K. Over the past five years, the University has generated 148 Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs), including 62 product patents and five global patents, besides supporting 115 student startups and more than 130 commercialised products.

Speaking during the session, Vice Chancellor, Prof Nazir.
A Ganai SKUAST-K, highlighted the need to accelerate technological interventions in agriculture to unlock the sector’s untapped potential.

He said while the Green Revolution helped India overcome food shortages, the country now needs to focus on technology, skilled human resources and innovation to address emerging agricultural challenges.
The Vice Chancellor also underlined concerns related to technological and data sovereignty in agriculture, particularly with the increasing use of drones, sensors and digital platforms.
He stressed that farmers’ rights must extend beyond markets, land and water to the digital domain as well.

The technical sessions featured addresses by Shri N.S. Rathore, Former Vice Chancellor, MPUAT, Udaipur, and Former Deputy Director General (Education), ICAR, on “AI-Driven Agricultural Technology, Smart Skills & Advanced Agricultural Techniques”, and Prof. V.P. Singh, Distinguished Professor, Texas.

A&M University, USA, on “Mathematical Modelling of the Water-Energy-Environment-Food Nexus.” The session also highlighted the research and innovation ecosystem of SKUAST-K. Over the past five years, the University has generated 148 Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs), including 62 product patents and five global patents, besides supporting 115 student startups and more than 130 commercialised products.

The convention focused on themes including ‘Women Leading Engineering Innovations in Smart Farming’ and ‘AI and Robotics for Gen-Z Farming’.

stories.headline: Supreme Court revives grower's claim after police destroyed $37K legal hemp
stories.title: Supreme Court revives grower's claim after police destroyed $37K legal hemp
stories.summary: In 2021, Georgia police aircraft allegedly destroyed $37,000 worth of legally grown hemp during a drug-suppression operation. Six years later, the Georgia Supreme Court revived the grower’s compensation claim, overturning a 60-year-old precedent that broadly shielded government agencies from property-damage claims when acting under police powers. The ruling allows the lawsuit to proceed, though damages have not yet been awarded.

stories.headline: Cabinet celebrates Modi’s 25-year head of Govt run
stories.title: Cabinet celebrates Modi’s 25-year head of Govt run
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 6: The Union Cabinet on Tuesday passed a resolution congratulating Prime Minister NarendraModi on completing 25 years of continuous leadership as head of government. Far more than a customary tribute, it celebrated the extraordinary journey of PM Modi guided by principle of 'Nation First and Citizen First'. The resolution said that three overwhelming mandates in Gujarat and support in three successive LokSabha elections reflect the enduring trust that public have reposed in PM NarendraModi. The ten salient features of the resolution capture the unbroken thread connecting his leadership of Gujarat with his leadership of India. The resolution traces how PM Modi carried Gujarat’s successful initiatives to the national stage. SWAGAT, through which he personally heard citizens’ grievances, received the United Nations Public Service Award in 2010. It later inspired PRAGATI, bringing governments together to review stalled projects, resolve obstacles and accelerate completion. Jyotigram’s separate agricultural electricity feeders similarly became a national approach, extending Gujarat’s experience across India. The resolution said that PM Modi’s sensitivity towards poverty grew from watching his mother struggle with everyday hardships and encountering deprivation during his travels. The resolution connects these experiences with programmes delivering homes, water, banking and healthcare. Nearly 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts, over 4 crore homes and 25 crore people moving out of poverty show how personal understanding became public action, bringing families dignity. The resolution said that PM Modi’s determination to help people shape their futures runs through the resolution. Approximately 3.5 crore women became Lakhpati Didis, while the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam provided for women’s reservation. Startups, skills and education reform expanded youth opportunities. PM-KISAN transfers exceeded Rs 4 lakh crore, while PM-JANMAN brought focused support to particularly vulnerable tribal communities, extending development to those historically left behind. The resolution gives particular emphasis to PM Modi’s willingness to pursue reform despite political risks. GST, welfare delivery reforms and the replacement of colonial laws demonstrate his determination to address longstanding challenges. The resolution said that his appeals on cleanliness, digital payments and local products drew citizens into change. It said that reform emerged as a sustained commitment of his leadership, strengthened by conviction, public participation and national purpose. The resolution said that under PM Modi’s leadership, public capital expenditure rose from Rs 2 lakh crore to over Rs 12 lakh crore, alongside highway expansion and railway electrification. Electronics production increased from around Rs 2 lakh crore to more than Rs 13 lakh crore. Defence production and semiconductor manufacturing further reflect his determination to strengthen India’s ability to meet its needs. The resolution said that PM Modi’s faith in technology emerges through achievements spanning everyday services and scientific frontiers. Jan Dhan, Aadhaar and mobile connectivity improved welfare delivery, while UPI transformed payments. The resolution said that developing India’s own COVID vaccines and landing Chandrayaan-3 near the Moon’s south pole demonstrated PM Modi’s vision of a scientifically capable, self-reliant, Atmanirbhar Bharat. Private space participation and work in artificial intelligence, quantum technology and biotechnology carry forward the vision celebrated in the resolution: technology improving lives while expanding national possibilities. The resolution highlights PM Modi’s ability to give India direction through global upheaval. During COVID, he united the country, backed domestic vaccine development and enabled rapid vaccination. During the West Asia crisis, timely decisions and energy security measures helped India withstand disruption. The resolution said that his leadership combined immediate responses with capabilities built over years, giving the country resilience and confidence in difficult times. It said that 2016 surgical strikes, 2019 Balakot air strikes, and 2025 Operation Sindoor illustrate the national security red lines established under PM Modi. The resolution places these alongside the removal of Article 370, 'One Rank One Pension' and creation of the Chief of Defence Staff’s post. It said action against Maoist terrorism and peace efforts in the Northeast bring out leadership combining national resolve with development, stability, and public trust. The resolution links India’s rising stature with PM Modi’s ability to build cooperation across divisions. Consensus at G20 and BRICS, advocacy for the Global South and the African Union’s G20 inclusion reflect his diplomatic leadership. Vaccine Maitri demonstrated how India’s capabilities could serve others. Honours from 36 countries underline the international regard accompanying PM Modi and India’s growing influence and contribution to shared solutions. The resolution said PM Modi’s vision unites development, cultural confidence, and environmental responsibility. Climate action progressed from Gujarat’s dedicated department to renewable energy expansion and international partnerships. Yoga, millets, Kashi Vishwanath Dham, and Ram Lalla’s consecration strengthened India’s connection with its heritage. The resolution culminated in renewed commitment to his vision of collective effort towards a prosperous, self-reliant, and developed India by 2047.

stories.headline: Population enumeration under census 2027 in snow bound areas of J&K, Ladakh concludes: CPCO
stories.title: Population enumeration under census 2027 in snow bound areas of J&K, Ladakh concludes: CPCO
stories.summary: Jammu, Oct 6: Chief Principal Census Officer (CPCO) and Director Census Operations (DCO), Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh Amit Sharma on Tuesday stated that the population enumeration, as part of Census 2027, was successfully completed in the designated snow-bound areas of Jammu and Kashmir Union Territory (UT) and entire Ladakh Union Territory from September 1 to 30, 2026. Amit Sharma, while addressing a press conference here, said that five-day revision round also concluded on October 5 to incorporate omissions, corrections so as to ensure no household was left out in the crucial decennial exercise. The population enumeration in the designated snow-bound areas, according to him, covered 5,292 Enumeration Blocks (EBs) including 4,597 in Jammu and Kashmir and 695 in Ladakh, involving enumeration across remote and difficult-to-access areas requiring extensive preparation, specialised field arrangements and close coordination with district administrations and Special Charges, CPCO said, while describing the successful completion as a significant milestone in the preparations for Census 2027. He maintained that the Army and Central Para Military Forces’ personnel were covered under Census 2027, with population enumeration of special charges completed through paper schedules in view of security concerns. “An important component of the exercise was enumeration in Special Charges including the Army, para military forces and other central forces. Population Enumeration was completed in 125 Special Charges of Defence and CAPFs in the snow-bound areas of J&K and 47 Special Charges in Ladakh. Dedicated arrangements were made for these locations, with paper schedules used for enumeration and operational doubts and queries being resolved in real time,” he said. CPCO shared that the concerned forces extended full support and supervision, while digitisation of the collected data was currently in progress. “As a very positive development, we had regular meetings with the Ministry of Defence. The Army, which has a very large presence among the Special Charges, is providing direct data to us through its central database,” he informed. Amit Sharma reiterated that that the census operation – a decennial exercise, conducted by the Ministry of Home Affairs through the office of the Registrar General and the Census Commissioner of India and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) – conducted by the Election Commission of India were entirely two separate exercises and one should not have any doubts between the two. Giving a detailed account of census operation, he shared that the snow-bound population enumeration was preceded by self-enumeration from August 17 to 31, 2026, followed by field operations from September 1 to 30, 2026. In Ladakh, the entire Union Territory was covered during the September exercise, with 695 Enumeration Blocks (EBs) completed—367 in Leh and 328 in Kargil. “With population enumeration now completed in UT of Ladakh, it has become the first in the entire country to complete population enumeration for Census 2027,” he said. In UT of J&K, according to him, the snow-bound operation covered 16 districts and 95 Charges. Doda recorded the highest number of completed EBs at 798, followed by Kishtwar with 602; Ramban with 418; Anantnag with 377 and Baramulla with 359. Reasi recorded 345 completed EBs and Udhampur 313. Kishtwar district was declared fully snow-bound and hence has become the first district in the entire country to complete population enumeration for Census 2027. CPCO Amit Sharma appreciated the coordinated efforts of the district administrations, census functionaries, Special Charges, enumerators and supervisors and the cooperation extended by residents. He observed that the completion of the exercise across difficult and remote terrain demonstrated the preparedness of the census machinery and the effectiveness of the field-level arrangements put in place for areas where geography and climatic conditions required a separate enumeration schedule. The successful field operation was backed by an extensive preparatory exercise. Nodal Officers and District Coordinators were deployed in the districts for field training, preparation and demarcation of Enumeration Blocks, distribution of census kits and ensuring that prescribed manuals reached the Charges, he asserted. Amit Sharma said that the exercise also received close attention from the senior leadership of the Census Organisation. Mritunjay Kumar Narayan, Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India, undertook visit to J&K in August and his maiden visit to Ladakh during September to personally review the implementation and progress of population enumeration in the snow-bound areas. Sunil Kumar, Additional Registrar General, visited J&K during the preparatory phase in August. Both senior officers expressed satisfaction with the progress of preparations, training and field operations, CPCO said. Amit Sharma also shared that the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India also deputed observers to monitor the population enumeration in snow-bound non-synchronous areas. The observers examined adherence to Census instructions and timelines, functioning of digital applications and devices, operational issues, respondent cooperation and the quality and progress of fieldwork, besides interacting with Principal Census Officers, Charge Officers, supervisors and enumerators. “Their field visits established the smooth conduct of the exercise and the officers from Delhi appreciated the timely completion of training, EB formation, distribution of materials, fieldwork and publicity activities,” he said. Amit Sharma especially mentioned that public participation was strengthened through a sustained multi-channel publicity campaign across the snow-bound areas. The outreach included advertisements in major newspapers, publicity vans with LED screens, banners at J&K Bank branches, pamphlet distribution, a seminar-cum-discussion at Bhaderwah campus of the University of Jammu, a quiz competition in Kishtwar, and radio jingles in Hindi, Urdu, Kashmiri and Dogri on Akashwani and Red FM. Hoardings were also installed at district headquarters, bus stands and other public places. “The campaign contributed to wider awareness, with residents extending enthusiastic cooperation to the enumerators and supervisors,” he said, adding, “With the snow-bound enumeration now concluded, the remaining population enumeration in the non-snow-bound areas of J&K is scheduled for February 2027.” Amit Sharma said that the Directorate would now focus on the prescribed post-enumeration processes for the completed areas while simultaneously ensuring that preparations for the February exercise in the remaining areas of J&K should remain on schedule. Ladakh, having completed population enumeration across the entire Union Territory, stands outside the February 2027 enumeration schedule. CPCO Amit Sharma shared that alongside population enumeration, work on the District Census Handbook (DCHB) was progressing in both Union Territories. Training for DCHB fieldwork was completed across all districts by September 27, 2026, while fieldwork was scheduled for completion by October 30, 2026. In J&K, the exercise involves 284 Charge Officers, 65 Town Officers and 2,854 Village Officers, while in Ladakh 17 Charge Officers, 2 Town Officers and 56 Village Officers have been engaged. The snow-bound operation was supported by substantial logistical and financial arrangements, with approximately Rs 49.2 Cr released to the respective districts for IT infrastructure, POL, contingency, honorarium and training allowances, he informed. Amit Sharma said that the completion of the snow-bound operation represented an important step in the phased conduct of Census 2027, while stressing that the focus would remain on data quality, completeness and adherence to prescribed procedures through the subsequent stages. The final population figures for Ladakh and the snow-bound areas of J&K will form part of the nationwide Census results, which are scheduled to be released after completion of the overall Census exercise in March–April 2027.
